y0079ff76f2c.add: - **Gramadevata (village goddess) shrines:** belong to the **Shakta (Sakteya)** tradition of mother-goddess worship – not Saiva, Pancharatra or Jaina (APPSC Endowment 2022).

y20d1583564f.add: - **Faiths of the age:** Shaivism, Vaishnavism, Jainism and (declining) Buddhism coexisted under the Eastern Chalukyas; **Judaism** was not among them.

gb78e8ddabf36.add: - **Councils:** the Eastern Chalukya councils were called **Varagoshti**; the **Yuvaraja** was a partner in governance.

y63f6e7fa0b8.add: - **Temple → location match:** Draksharamam – **Konaseema**; Srisailam – **Kurnool** (now Nandyal district); Brihadisvara – **Thanjavur**; Sri Mukhalingeswara – **Srikakulam**.

y86feb119ff7.add: - **Ambapuram and Adavi Nekkalam hills** (north-east of Vijayawada): repositories of rock-cut **Jain caves** (7th–8th c.), incl. the Ambapuram cave temple with a Mahavira image.

yf164eb9afa1.add: - **Durjaya lineage:** the Velanati chiefs claimed descent from the **Durjaya** family, called themselves **Chaturthanvaya** (of the fourth, i.e. Sudra, caste) and were loyal feudatories of the **Chalukya-Cholas** after the Eastern Chalukya decline.

ya9933269c0e.add: - **Battle of Manneru:** **Kulottunga II**, sent to Vengi by Vikrama Chola, with the chiefs of **Velanadu, Giripaschima and Konakandravadi** drove out the **Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas** in the battle of **Manneru**.

ya12d3dd7e47.add: - **Cultural impact on South-East Asia:** India exported **Buddhism, Sanskrit and temple architecture** (Angkor, Borobudur) – but **not the hierarchical caste system**.

y72df689c371.add: - **Match:** Chola bronzes – **patronage of Chola kings**; Nataraja – **masterpiece of Chola bronzes**; Shiva Tandava – **cosmic symbolism** (creation, preservation, destruction); Devadasi system – **integral to temple rituals**.

yd33c26640d6.add: - **Kamban:** wrote the Tamil Ramayana (Ramavataram) at the court of the **Chola** king **Kulottunga III** – not the Hoysalas, Pandyas or Cheras.

y8d8e8068785.add: - **Temple → dynasty match:** Lingaraja, Bhubaneswar – **(Eastern) Ganga** in exam keys; Vaikuntha Perumal, Kanchipuram – **Pallava**; Brihadisvara, Thanjavur – **Chola**; Chennakeshava, Belur – **Hoysala**.

y7e09a441649.add: - **Greatest Kakatiya:** **Ganapatideva** largely restored the **political unity of the Telugu country**; he had **two daughters**, **Rudramadevi** and **Ganapamba (Ganapamadevi)**.

y01643a705dc.add: - **Prominence:** Rudramadevi is reckoned among the **most prominent Kakatiya rulers**; inscriptions style her a **king** (Rudradeva Maharaja) – from **1258** in co-regency, sole rule from **1262**.

y94ce7691447.add: - **Not a son-in-law:** **Recherla Prasaditya Nayaka** was Rudrama's general and protector (Kakatiya-rajya-sthapanacharya), not her son-in-law; her sons-in-law were **Mahadeva, Ellanadeva and Induluri Annaya**.

yac18d4ac9f8.add: - **Historian's verdict:** **P.V. Parabrahma Sastry** pointed out that **Kannada (Chalukya) rule in Andhra ended** with the establishment of the Kakatiya kingdom.

y15df574e6cd.add: - **Standard text:** **(Veera Saiva) Siddhanta Shikhamani** of **Shivayogi Shivacharya** is regarded as the complete and standard scripture of Veerashaivism; Basava Puranam is a biography of Basava.

yfe691c77b81.add: - **Pairs (C and D ✓):** Uddanda Raya – **Uddandarayunipalem** (Amaravati); Rudramba – **devotee of Shiva**; ✗ Amuktamalyada is a **Vaishnava** poem of Krishnadevaraya, not a Buddhist discourse, and Kalachakra is not linked to Harihara Raya.

y7764cba5ffe.add: - **Saraswati Gachchas:** set up by the **Jains** to spread education among the common people.

gc9a06171254b.add: - **Saraswati Gachchas:** set up by the **Jains** to spread education among the common people.

y77a1f21f4b6.add: - **Dommaras:** by their own claim the Dommaras (acrobats) of medieval Andhra had **24 sub-castes** (printed key, not verified).

y78b35d50d38.add: - **Yaganti** (Uma Maheswara temple, Vijayanagara period): **Kurnool district** – now in **Nandyal district** (since 4 Apr 2022).

y006343af2c3.add: - **Anantavarman Chodaganga** (1078–1147): **Eastern Ganga** king of **Kalinga (Orissa)** who began the **Jagannath temple, Puri** – the Gangas preceded the Gajapatis.

yc0838e8704a.add: - **Perantallu:** women who committed **sati** were deified as demi-goddesses and worshipped as **Perantallu** in Reddi-period Andhra.

nc56226823b2.add: - **Move to Rajahmundry:** after Kondaveedu fell (1424), Srinatha reached **Veerabhadra Reddi's** court through the minister **Bendapudi Anantamatya**.

n63b62c72cec.add: - **Chatu verses:** after Rajahmundry fell (1448), Srinatha's chatu padyalu portray the **hard life and coarse food of poverty-stricken Palnadu**.

fefea56cd5ebc.add: - **Palnati Veera Charitra** (dvipada) narrates the **Palnadu war of 1182** (battle of Karempudi).

yba80959860f.add: - **Succession in the epic:** **Yudhishthira** crowned **Parikshit** (Abhimanyu's son) before his last journey; Janamejaya was Parikshit's son.

y6e02c85e9d5.add: - **Origin debate:** **Chilukuri Narayana Rao** (Andhra Bhasha Charitramu) held that Telugu was born of **Sanskrit** and the Prakrits; **Bishop Caldwell** held it Dravidian.

yfabffb569c8.add: - **Classical languages in order:** Tamil (2004), **Sanskrit (2005)**, Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014); Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali (3 Oct 2024) → **11**.

yf9234d5699a.add: - **Gujari Mahal, Gwalior:** built by **Raja Man Singh Tomar** (1486–1516) for his Gujar queen **Mrignayani**.

y7d0b0844267.add: - **The word:** **Rajput** comes from **Rajaputra** (son of a ruler); they were warrior lineages claiming **Kshatriya** status (8th–14th c.).

y059c79cd69c.add: - **"Who finally devastated the Cholas?"** – books and keys say **Malik Kafur** (1311 raid on the far south); strictly the Chola line had already ended in **1279** under the Pandyas.

yd6c01e18173.add: - **Palace of a thousand pillars** (Qasr-i-Hazar Sutun, at **Siri**): built by **Alauddin Khalji** – not the Kakatiya Thousand Pillar temple.

y2867bf22731.add: - **Carpets (17th–18th c.):** Andhra carpet-making (**Eluru, Masulipatnam**, also Warangal, Kurnool) grew under **Persian immigrant weavers** – not a purely local Krishna–Godavari craft; varieties **Bulbandi, Nabashkhany, Gopalraokhany**.

n2959e8d2e14.add: - **Kuchipudi:** the dance grew under **Siddhendra Yogi**; **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** granted the village of **Kuchipudi** to its dancers (1678).

n6bbc94b2f4d.add: - **Kuchipudi:** the dance grew under **Siddhendra Yogi**; **Abul Hasan Tana Shah** granted the village of **Kuchipudi** to its dancers (1678).

yfe6b3e74039.add: - **Jaimini Bharatam:** by **Pillalamarri Pina Veerabhadrudu**, contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** – not Krishnadevaraya or Gona Budda Reddy.

yef9e796392f.add: - **Jaimini Bharatam:** by **Pillalamarri Pina Veerabhadrudu**, contemporary of **Saluva Narasimha** – not Krishnadevaraya or Gona Budda Reddy.

ycdeef61c22c.add: - **Rayavachakam** (Telugu prose, by **Sthanapati**): describes **Krishnadevaraya's court and daily life**.

ya5e93bc3798.add: - **Statements (I and III ✓):** Vijayanagara markets dealt in **spices, textiles and precious stones**; **amara-nayakas** were military commanders given territories by the Rayas; ✗ Krishnadevaraya's reign was **not** marked by strain within the imperial structure – it was the empire's peak.

y009f724904f.add: - **Krishnadevaraya's taxation (UPSC 2016 – both ✓):** land-tax rate **fixed by the quality of the land**; **private owners of workshops paid an industries tax**.

yb4532d17d19.add: - **Crops of the age:** **coconut** (native to the Indian coasts) was grown; **groundnut, tobacco and red chilli** are American crops brought later by the Portuguese.

y93dd0fd3ec4.add: - **Not Andhra:** **Lavani** (dance-song with the dholki, part of **Tamasha**) is from **Maharashtra**.

y42a33665128.add: - **Nautanki** (Uttar Pradesh folk theatre): two schools – **Hathras** and **Kanpur**.

ya7b04a55348.add: - **Ali Bakhshi Khyal:** Rajasthani khyal theatre of **Alwar**, founded by Ali Bakhsh of Mandawar.

ye463eca6993.add: - **Abhinaya Darpanam** (Sanskrit treatise on gesture in dance): by **Nandikeshvara** – Natyashastra is Bharata's, Nritta Ratnavali Jayapa's.

y73393b4650b.add: - **Pandit Birju Maharaj** (Lucknow gharana): widely called the face / father of modern **Kathak**.

y03e09073c39.add: - **Tamasha** proper is the Lavani-based folk theatre of **Maharashtra**; the Jaipur Tamasha of the Bhatt family is a Rajasthani offshoot.

yd4fb9d2a69d.add: - **Giddha:** women's folk dance of **Punjab** – a "Giddha – Gujarat" pair is wrong.

y6039274cf0a.add: - **State festival, 2016:** the tribal **Sri Sri Sri Modakondamma Talli Jatara** of **Paderu** (ASR district).

y2af935c3f31.add: - **Sangidi rallu** (stone-lifting / balancing sport): linked to **Vizianagaram** (printed key, not verified).

ye45341a047f.add: - **Onam:** Kerala's harvest festival, in the Malayalam month of **Chingam = August–September**.

y3583d1af93d.add: - **Butta Bommalu:** light wooden (papier-mâché-like) toys of **Tanuku, West Godavari** – the **Godavari districts**.

y5a6a1cccece.add: - **Dhanu Jatra:** world's largest open-air theatre festival (Krishna and Kansa) at **Bargarh, western Odisha**.

ye139c216c0c.add: - **Chandanotsavam, Simhachalam:** the sandal paste of Sri Varaha Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy is removed for **Nijaroopa darshan** and fresh sandalwood paste applied on **Akshaya Tritiya**.

y44f8d066109.add: - **Sufi link:** Babur was a follower of the **Naqshbandi** saint **Khwaja Ubaidullah Ahrar**; the order came to India with him.

yece4369c785.add: - **Empire as a political fact:** under **Akbar** (1556–1605) the Mughal empire, consolidated by conquest, mansabdari and the Rajput policy, became a lasting political fact and factor in Indian life.

yc49faf96431.add: - **Shah Jahan's court and faith:** abolished **sijda** (prostration, begun by Balban) for the chahar taslim; dropped Akbar's solar **Ilahi** era and restored the **Hijri** reckoning; slightly **more orthodox** than Akbar – destroyed some newly built temples, yet kept many Hindu nobles.

y09c617a8847.add: - **Jahangir's memoirs and bans:** wrote the **Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri in Persian** (Babur's memoirs were in Turki); **banned tobacco** smoking (1617).

na3fa9b107e7.add: - **Title:** Jahangir gave Prince **Khurram** the title **'Shah Jahan' = 'King of the World'** (Alamgir = Conqueror of the World – Aurangzeb).

nindian-history-11-14.add: - **Title:** Jahangir gave Prince **Khurram** the title **'Shah Jahan' = 'King of the World'** (Alamgir = Conqueror of the World – Aurangzeb).

n7559667ccbf.add: - **Religious policy:** Jahangir broadly continued **Akbar's tolerance**; Guru Arjan Dev's execution (1606) was political – for backing Khusrau.

f4f49b6e3b13d.add: - **Majma-ul-Bahrain** ('mingling of two oceans'), by **Dara Shikoh**: compares **Sufism and Vedanta**.

nindian-history-23-10.add: - **Jizya exemptions:** women, **children below 14**, slaves, beggars and the unemployed.

ya503c795baf.add: - **Radha Govind Sangeet Sar:** the great music treatise of Jaipur, credited to **Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh** (r. 1778–1803); some books credit its compilation to his court scholar Devarshi Brajpal Bhatt.

n01749b737e2.add: - **Religious policy and alienation:** Aurangzeb's policies, incl. the **reimposition of jizya (1679)**, alienated the **Rajputs, Marathas and Sikhs**.

faaa84bae9134.add: - **Third Panipat:** **14 January 1761** – Abdali beat the Marathas (Karnal, 24 Feb 1739, was Nadir Shah's).

f7493ac3464c7.add: - **Hyderabad's autonomy:** **Nizam-ul-Mulk** became autonomous after defeating **Mubariz Khan at Shakarkheda (1724)**.

gdffeaa4db464.add: - **Treaty of Allahabad (1765):** after Buxar, **Shah Alam II** granted the **Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa** to the East India Company.

nf2f1e10e0ad.add: - **Chola patronage of the Nayanars:** **Rajaraja I** consecrated bronzes of all **63 Nayanmars at Chidambaram**; Parantaka I had installed statues of Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar.

g193f4c3a4269.add: - **Tevaram** (hymns of Appar, Sambandar, Sundarar) = the **earliest and most sacred** part (books 1–7) of the Tirumurai.

y2c9b4c9aafc.add: - **Kabir's verses survive in three traditions:** the **Bijak** (Kabirpanth, Varanasi), the **Kabir Granthavali** (Dadupanth, Rajasthan) and the **Adi Granth Sahib**.

y6c29c8ce712.add: - **Odd man out (Carnatic):** Maharajapuram Viswanatha Iyer, Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and Musiri Subramania Iyer were **vocalists**; **T.R. Mahalingam** was a **flautist**.

y61ff3475335.add: - **Pre-1789 French taxes:** the **tithe** (about one-tenth of produce) went to the **Church**; the **taille** was the direct tax paid to the state.

y494a30a842a.add: - **February Revolution (1917):** began in **Petrograd** (St Petersburg); the **October Revolution** of 25 Oct 1917 (Julian) = **7 November 1917** (Gregorian).

y73f157b0fe3.add: - **February Revolution (1917):** began in **Petrograd** (St Petersburg); the **October Revolution** of 25 Oct 1917 (Julian) = **7 November 1917** (Gregorian).

ydd9561e22db.add: - **Fort St. David:** English fort at **Devanampatnam (Tegnapatnam) near Cuddalore**, bought in **1690**.

y5f148643877.add: - **Hornby Vellard:** sea wall closing the Worli breach, approved by Governor **William Hornby** (1771–84), completed 1784.

ycd08f84da56.add: - **Pre-colonial economy:** Andhra's dominant activity was **textile production** and export – Masulipatnam chintz and calico.

yf400423b6ac.add: - **First Golconda farman for a Masulipatnam factory:** the **Dutch** (1605–06), not the Portuguese; Masulipatnam rose as a maritime centre in the **last quarter of the 16th century**.

nbcb6b31688d.add: - **Why Travancore mattered:** a **British ally** and the Company's **only pepper supplier** – Tipu's attack (1789) precipitated the Third war.

n7d4010c3500.add: - **British fear behind the Fourth war:** **Lord Wellesley** feared Tipu's alliance with **Napoleon** (then in Egypt) and the French.

nd88f62819fd.add: - **Spice factor:** British conflicts with Mysore were driven partly by Mysore's control of Malabar **pepper and cardamom**, its threat to Madras and its French ties.

n0763ccc365e.add: - **First war alliance:** the **Nizam, the Marathas and the British** were at first allied against **Haidar Ali** (Haidar later detached the Nizam).

y9cd5c87c5a0.add: - **Mulki rules:** local-candidate conditions for state posts were introduced in **1888** under **Mir Mahbub Ali Khan** (6th Nizam) and tightened by Mir Osman Ali Khan's farman of 1919.

n9cec66a8174.add: - **Pretext for 1801:** the Carnatic Nawab's Nellore and Chittoor lands were annexed on the charge of **collusion with Tipu Sultan**.

ged1430fe5ed9.add: - **How the Nizam got them:** after the Third Mysore War, the **Treaty of Seringapatam (1792)** gave Nizam Ali **Bellary, Gandikota and Kadapa** (half the Rayalaseema lands) from Tipu.

y6cc21acf1bf.add: - **Settlement with Narayana Babu:** the Vizianagaram estate was restored to him after negotiations with the Company; he agreed to pay arrears of about **Rs 5 lakh** (printed A–R key: both true, R not the explanation).

y3e86f26a319.add: - **Colonial Andhra (statement PYQ, key 1, 3, 4):** the Northern Circars passed from the French to the English (1759–66) under the **Madras Presidency**; Andhra joined the **NCM and CDM**; ✗ "1857 had no impact" – there were risings in 1857–58 (e.g. the **Gulugonda** tribal rising, Visakhapatnam).

y7654178d19a.add: - **A–R angle:** Company rule was revenue-driven and **neglected irrigation for long** (A ✗); Cotton's anicuts on the **Godavari (1847)** and **Krishna (1853)** were the major exceptions (R ✓).
